title: Suspected Cases Surpass 1,000 — Total 1,077 Suspected, 246 Probable Deaths as Outbreak Enters Critical Phase
detail: As of 31 May 2026, suspected Ebola cases from the ongoing Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak in DRC and Uganda surpassed 1,000 for the first time, with CGTN and WHO tracking data indicating 1,077 total suspected cases — a significant acceleration from 906 suspected cases in WHO Situation Report #2 on 26 May. DRC accounted for 1,028 suspected cases, while Uganda had 9 lab-confirmed cases (1 confirmed death). Probable deaths reached 246 across the outbreak, including approximately 220 suspected DRC deaths and 26 confirmed deaths. The 1,000-case threshold was reached just 14 days after the WHO PHEIC declaration on 17 May 2026 — a pace exceeding the 2018–2020 Kivu outbreak's early trajectory. Three key transmission drivers continued on 31 May: (1) The Mongbwalu escaped-patient cluster remained partially at large, with DRC MoH estimating 18–22 of the original 25+ escaped patients had now been relocated to isolation or were confirmed dead in the community — generating uncounted community transmission events; (2) Contact tracing coverage in Ituri remained below 50%, far short of the 80% needed for containment; (3) The WHO expert panel ring vaccination ruling (28 May) had suspended Ervebo use, creating a 6–12 week vaccine gap before any BDBV-specific clinical trial vaccine becomes available. WHO's emergency R&D team was reported working urgently on an accelerated trial protocol for ChAdOx1 BDBV at Bunia and Kampala sites. Epidemic modelers tracking the outbreak projected that without re-establishment of ETU coverage in Mongbwalu and contact tracing above 70%, total cases could exceed 3,000 by mid-June 2026.

title: WHO DG Issues 'Maximum Mobilization' Emergency Appeal — Calls for Accelerated Clinical Trial Framework After DRC Visit
detail: Following his in-person visit to Bunia and Kinshasa on 30 May 2026, WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus issued an Emergency Appeal on 31 May 2026, calling on all member states and international partners for 'maximum mobilization' to avert a catastrophic escalation of the 2026 BDBV outbreak. The appeal cited the 1,000-case threshold breach and the imminent vaccine gap created by the 28 May WHO expert panel ruling that halted rVSV-ZEBOV (Ervebo) off-label ring vaccination. Key asks in the appeal: (1) Immediate contributions to WHO's Emergency Contingency Fund target of $200M for the BDBV response — the fund had reached $47M as of late May, leaving a $153M gap; (2) Accelerated review of ChAdOx1 BDBV clinical trial protocol at proposed Bunia/Kampala sites, with WHO committing to regulatory fast-track support; (3) CEPI and Gavi contributions to production scale-up for ChAdOx1 BDBV and rVSV BDBV (IAVI) vaccine candidates; (4) Additional ETU capacity and field epidemiology surge in Mongbwalu; (5) UNSC engagement on humanitarian access in Ituri, citing 23% zone inaccessibility. The appeal also urged neighboring countries — Rwanda, South Sudan, Burundi, Tanzania — to maintain enhanced health screening at open borders rather than following Uganda's closure model, reiterating WHO IHR guidance. France, the UK, and Germany announced they were reviewing requests for additional funding contributions in response to the DG appeal.
